method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula/macro/reference comparison, reverse paraphrase and bounded primary-source terminology research; not independent or human review.
scope: All twenty-six translated blocks in the ordered-rings-and-fields appendix, including every axiom, proof, exercise, footnote and cut calculation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The constructed integers should form a commutative ring. The eight displayed laws define that structure, and representative calculations establish associativity, additive inverses and distributivity while relying on arithmetic of naturals.
samples.checks: All eight equations, implicit universal restriction, warning about the meanings of zero and one, representative choices, equivalence-class notation and every equality in the three proofs are preserved exactly.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The integer order must make an ordered ring; the footnote recalls total-order properties and trichotomy. Adding nonzero multiplicative inverses gives an ordered field, which rationals should satisfy, while reals must additionally satisfy completeness.
samples.checks: The order-reference target, four relation properties, disjunction, two compatibility implications, ordered-field label, inverse quantifiers, completeness reference and all three number-system distinctions remain present.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Real addition must produce a cut. The proof shows the sum is a nonempty proper rational subset, is downward closed, and has no maximum. Similar checks are assigned for subtraction, multiplication and nonzero division before the ordered-field exercise.
samples.checks: Every witness, inequality and membership step is retained. MRARITH-008 discloses that subtraction and division formulas were left inactive upstream without inventing a replacement definition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The rationals below square root of two form a cut. For a positive p below the root, q=(2p+2)/(p+2) is both larger than p and still has square below two, so the cut has no maximum.
samples.checks: The set-builder disjunction, q definition and every line in both inequality chains have exact formula parity.

source_observations.finding: A noun is missing in the source's phrase introducing the tedious ordered-field check.
source_observations.resolution: The intended generic checking noun is supplied in Marathi and documented adjacent to the sentence.

source_observations.finding: The appendix presupposes subtraction and division definitions that remain inactive comments in the source cuts section.
source_observations.resolution: The exercise is translated faithfully with an adjacent disclosure; no unsupported operation definition is activated.

limitations: No independent linguistic or mathematical certification has been performed.
